questions.q: Which term is used generally for a sacred grove in the Khasi Hills of Meghalaya, as distinct from the Jaintia term Khloo Blai?
o: Khloo Blai
Khlaw Kyntang
Asong Khosi
Niam Tre
questions.e: The Meghalaya Biodiversity Board identifies Khlaw Kyntang, Law Kyntang and Law Lyngdoh as general Khasi-Hills terms for sacred groves. Khloo Blai is the Jaintia-Hills term, while Asong Khosi is associated with Garo usage; Niam Tre refers to a traditional religious belief rather than the general grove term.
questions.source: Original Practice — not an official PYQ. Meghalaya Biodiversity Board — Sacred Groves.

questions.q: Under Section 37 of the Biological Diversity Act, 2002, which authority may notify an area of biodiversity importance as a Biodiversity Heritage Site?
o: The State Government in consultation with local bodies
The National Biodiversity Authority acting alone
The district police administration
A village committee without State Government notification
questions.e: Section 37 empowers the State Government, after consultation with local bodies, to notify biodiversity-important areas as Biodiversity Heritage Sites in the Official Gazette. The consultation requirement and the State Government's notification role are both essential parts of the provision.

questions.q: The Meghalaya Biodiversity Board describes a twin drainage system in the State. Which pairing is correct?
o: Barak in the north and Brahmaputra in the south
Brahmaputra in the north and Barak in the south
Teesta in the north and Subansiri in the south
Ganga in the north and Meghna in the south
questions.e: The Meghalaya Biodiversity Board describes the Brahmaputra system to the north and the Barak system to the south. The State's relief and watershed pattern divide drainage broadly between these two major river systems.

questions.q: Which statement about Nepenthes khasiana, an insectivorous plant of Meghalaya, is correct according to the Meghalaya Biodiversity Board?
o: It is endemic to Meghalaya and listed in CITES Appendix I
It is native only to the Western Ghats and listed in Appendix II
It is an introduced aquatic plant with no conservation listing
It is endemic to the Andaman Islands and listed in Appendix III
questions.e: The Meghalaya Biodiversity Board states that Nepenthes khasiana is endemic to Meghalaya, appears in CITES Appendix I and is placed in Schedule VI of the Wildlife (Protection) Act, 1972. These details distinguish it from the other insectivorous plants mentioned on the Board's page.

questions.q: Which pair is identified in the Meghalaya Biodiversity Board's threatened-fauna table as endemic and rare amphibians of Meghalaya?
o: Bufoides meghalayanus and Pseudophilautus shillongensis
Philautus garo and Rana tigrina
Duttaphrynus melanostictus and Hoplobatrachus tigerinus
Euphlyctis cyanophlyctis and Kaloula pulchra
questions.e: The Board's threatened-fauna table lists Bufoides meghalayanus and Pseudophilautus shillongensis as endemic and rare in Meghalaya. The table gives Philautus shillongensis as the synonym for the latter species, so both names refer to the same Shillong bubble-nest frog.

questions.topic: CGST Section 72 — assistance to proper officers
questions.q: A proper officer is carrying out GST functions and seeks statutory assistance from another public department. Which statement best reflects Section 72 of the CGST Act?
o: Only private banks are required to assist
Police, railways, customs, land-revenue and specified State/UT tax officers are among those required to assist
Only the Registrar of Companies may assist
Assistance is voluntary for every public officer
questions.e: Section 72 requires specified officers, including police, railways, customs, land-revenue and State/Union-territory tax officers, to assist proper officers in implementing the Act. It is a statutory cooperation provision, not a general request to private bodies.

questions.q: A taxable person applies to pay an amount determined under the CGST Act in instalments. The amount is not liability self-assessed in a return. What is the maximum number of monthly instalments the Commissioner may allow under Section 80?
questions.e: Section 80 permits the Commissioner, for reasons recorded in writing, to allow monthly instalments not exceeding twenty-four. The facility does not cover an amount due as per liability self-assessed in a return, and interest under Section 50 remains payable subject to the prescribed conditions.

questions.q: Subject to the Insolvency and Bankruptcy Code, 2016, what status does Section 82 give to tax, interest or penalty payable under the CGST Act?
o: It is always an unsecured personal loan
It is a first charge on the property of the person liable
It ranks ahead of every claim even where the IBC provides otherwise
It becomes payable only after criminal conviction
questions.e: Section 82 makes the amount payable on account of tax, interest or penalty a first charge on the liable person's property. The section expressly preserves the exception where the Insolvency and Bankruptcy Code, 2016 provides otherwise, so the charge is not absolute against the IBC.

questions.q: An officer proposes to publish information obtained under Sections 150 or 151 in a way that identifies a particular taxable person. What does Section 152 generally require?
o: Only oral permission from any colleague
Previous written consent of the concerned person or authorised representative
Automatic publication after 30 days
Approval from the police station
questions.e: Section 152 bars publication that identifies a particular person without previous written consent of that person or the authorised representative. The Act also restricts use of such information in proceedings without giving the person concerned an opportunity of being heard; publication of a class of persons or transactions in the public interest is treated separately.

questions.q: During a lawful GST examination, the Commissioner considers it necessary to take a sample of goods from a taxable person's possession. What must be provided for the sample taken under Section 154?
o: A receipt
A tax invoice issued by the officer
A court decree
A fresh registration certificate
questions.e: Section 154 authorises the Commissioner or an officer authorised by the Commissioner to take samples of goods from a taxable person's possession when considered necessary. The provision specifically requires a receipt for any samples so taken, creating a record of the sample collection.

questions.topic: CGST Section 169 — service through common portal
questions.q: A GST notice is made available to the addressee on the common portal. Is this a recognised method of service under Section 169?
o: No; only personal hand delivery is valid
Yes; making the communication available on the common portal is an expressly listed mode
No; a notice must always be published in two newspapers
Yes, but only after the recipient signs a paper acknowledgement
questions.e: Section 169(1)(d) expressly recognises making a decision, order, summons, notice or other communication available on the common portal as a mode of service. Other listed modes include delivery, post or courier, registered e-mail, newspaper publication and specified forms of affixation.

questions.q: An amount payable under the CGST Act is ₹8,725.50. Applying Section 170, what is the rounded amount?
o: ₹8,725.50 must remain unchanged
questions.e: Section 170 rounds tax, interest, penalty, fine and other sums to the nearest rupee. A fractional part of fifty paise or more is increased to one rupee; a fraction below fifty paise is ignored. Therefore ₹8,725.50 becomes ₹8,726.

questions.q: A provisional attachment order is made under Section 83 of the CGST Act. If it is not otherwise ceased or dealt with under the Act, after what period does the attachment cease to have effect?
o: Three months
Six months
One year from the date of the order
Three years from the date of the order
questions.e: Section 83(2) states that every provisional attachment under the section ceases to have effect after one year from the date of the order. The attachment power is available only after initiation of proceedings under the specified chapters and when the Commissioner considers it necessary to protect government revenue.

questions.q: A bank holds money for a person who has failed to pay an amount due under the CGST Act. Which recovery step is expressly available under Section 79(1)(c)?
o: The proper officer may issue a written notice requiring the bank to pay the specified amount to the Government
The officer may cancel the bank's licence without process
The bank must transfer the taxpayer's entire balance regardless of the amount due
The officer must first obtain a criminal conviction
questions.e: Section 79(1)(c) permits the proper officer to issue a written notice to a person from whom money is due or who holds money for the defaulter. The notice requires payment to the Government up to the amount specified; it is a statutory third-party recovery mechanism.

questions.q: Under Section 153 of the CGST Act, what is the minimum rank of an officer who may take assistance from an expert in a complex case?
o: Tax Assistant
Superintendent
Assistant Commissioner
Commissioner only
questions.e: Section 153 allows any officer not below the rank of Assistant Commissioner to take expert assistance, having regard to the nature and complexity of the case and the interest of revenue. The assistance may be taken at the scrutiny, inquiry, investigation or other proceeding stage.

questions.topic: CGST Section 158A — consent for outward-supply data
questions.q: For sharing details of outward supplies furnished under Section 37 through the common portal under Section 158A, whose consent must be obtained?
o: Only the GST Network
Only the supplier
The supplier and the recipient
Neither party, because portal data is automatically public
questions.e: Section 158A(2) requires the supplier's consent for the listed details and also the recipient's consent for details under clause (b), which includes outward-supply information. The recipient-consent rule is an important distinction from data categories that concern only the supplier.

Only taxpayers' trade associations
Only State Legislatures
Only the High Courts

questions.topic: CGST Section 89 — directors of private companies
questions.q: Assuming a private company has not been converted into a public company, when may a director become jointly and severally liable for its GST dues under Section 89?
o: Whenever the director resigns after the demand is issued
Where the company's dues cannot be recovered, unless the director proves the non-recovery was not attributable to the director's gross neglect, misfeasance or breach of duty
Only when every shareholder gives written consent
Only when the company has no bank account
questions.e: Section 89 makes directors who held office during the relevant period jointly and severally liable where the private company's tax, interest or penalty cannot be recovered. A director can rebut this by proving to the Commissioner's satisfaction that the non-recovery was not attributable to the director's gross neglect, misfeasance or breach of duty; subsection (2) addresses conversion into a public company.

questions.q: Choose the correct completion: “No sooner had the file been received ___ the officer began the review.”
o: when
than
then
while
questions.e: The fixed correlative construction is “no sooner ... than”. The first clause commonly uses the past perfect, with inversion of the auxiliary “had” before the subject. “When” is paired with “hardly” or “scarcely”, not with “no sooner”.
questions.source: Original Practice — not an official PYQ. Cambridge Dictionary — English Grammar Today.
questions.label: Original Practice
questions.sourceName: Cambridge Dictionary — English Grammar Today

questions.q: Choose the correct verb: “The number of applications received this month ___ increased.”
o: have
has
are
were
questions.e: The grammatical subject is “the number”, which is singular, so it takes “has”. The plural noun “applications” appears inside the prepositional phrase and does not control the verb. Compare “a number of applications have increased”, where “a number” means several.
questions.source: Original Practice — not an official PYQ. Purdue OWL — Grammar and Subject–Verb Agreement.
questions.label: Original Practice
questions.sourceName: Purdue OWL — Grammar and Subject–Verb Agreement

questions.q: Choose the correct completion: “Each of the records ___ checked before dispatch.”
o: have been
has been
were
are being
questions.e: “Each” is grammatically singular even when it is followed by “of” and a plural noun. The correct singular auxiliary is “has”, giving “has been checked”. The nearby plural word “records” does not change the agreement rule.
questions.source: Original Practice — not an official PYQ. Purdue OWL — Grammar and Subject–Verb Agreement.

questions.q: Choose the correct completion: “Had the department issued the notice earlier, the hearing ___ completed before the deadline.”
o: will have been
would have been
would be
has been
questions.e: “Had the department issued” is an inverted form of “If the department had issued”. In a third conditional, the result clause normally uses “would have” plus the past participle; the passive form is therefore “would have been completed”.
questions.source: Original Practice — not an official PYQ. Cambridge Dictionary — English Grammar Today.
questions.label: Original Practice

questions.q: Choose the correct completion: “The more carefully returns are reconciled, ___ the risk of error becomes.”
o: the lower
lower than
the lowest
as low
questions.e: The paired comparative structure is “the more ..., the lower ...”. Both clauses express a corresponding change: increasing care in reconciliation is associated with a decreasing risk of error. “The lower” completes the second comparative clause correctly.
questions.source: Original Practice — not an official PYQ. Cambridge Dictionary — English Grammar Today.
questions.label: Original Practice
questions.sourceName: Cambridge Dictionary — English Grammar Today

questions.q: Choose the correct completion: “Despite ___ the figures twice, the clerk overlooked the mismatch.”
o: checked
checking
to check
checks
questions.e: “Despite” is a preposition, so it is followed by a noun phrase or a gerund phrase, not a finite verb in this construction. “Checking the figures twice” functions as the object of “despite”, making option B grammatically correct.

questions.topic: It is high time — past-tense form
questions.q: Choose the correct completion: “It is high time the office ___ its outdated register.”
o: replaces
replace
replaced
will replace
questions.e: The expression “it is high time” is conventionally followed by a past-tense form to express that an action is overdue, not that it happened only in the past. Therefore “replaced” is correct even though the intended action is needed now.

questions.q: How many positive divisors does 360 have?
questions.e: Prime-factorise 360 as 2³ × 3² × 5¹. For a number with prime powers pᵃqᵇrᶜ, the number of positive divisors is (a+1)(b+1)(c+1). Thus 360 has (3+1)(2+1)(1+1) = 4 × 3 × 2 = 24 positive divisors.
questions.source: Original Practice — not an official PYQ. NCERT — Mathematics Textbook Portal.
questions.label: Original Practice
questions.sourceName: NCERT — Mathematics Textbook Portal

questions.q: A invests ₹40,000 for 12 months and B invests ₹60,000 for 8 months. If profit is shared in proportion to capital multiplied by time, what is the ratio A:B?
questions.e: In a time-based partnership, each partner's profit share is proportional to capital × time. A's product is 40,000 × 12 = 4,80,000; B's is 60,000 × 8 = 4,80,000. The products are equal, so the profit-sharing ratio is 1:1.
questions.source: Original Practice — not an official PYQ. NCERT — Mathematics Textbook Portal.
questions.label: Original Practice
questions.sourceName: NCERT — Mathematics Textbook Portal

questions.q: How many distinct arrangements can be formed using all the letters of the word LEVEL?
questions.e: LEVEL has five letters, with L repeated twice and E repeated twice; V occurs once. The number of distinct arrangements is 5! divided by 2! for the repeated Ls and 2! for the repeated Es: 120 ÷ 4 = 30.
questions.source: Original Practice — not an official PYQ. NCERT — Mathematics Textbook Portal.

questions.q: What is the least common multiple of 3/4 and 9/10?
questions.e: For positive fractions in lowest terms, the least common multiple is the LCM of the numerators divided by the HCF of the denominators. LCM(3, 9) = 9 and HCF(4, 10) = 2, so the result is 9/2. It is divisible by both fractions: (9/2)/(3/4)=6 and (9/2)/(9/10)=5.
questions.source: Original Practice — not an official PYQ. NCERT — Mathematics Textbook Portal.
questions.label: Original Practice
questions.sourceName: NCERT — Mathematics Textbook Portal

questions.q: Statement: “The office has introduced a token system to reduce waiting time.” Which assumption is most directly implicit?
o: Visitors may be experiencing delays that an orderly queue could reduce
Every visitor already has a personal appointment
The office intends to reduce the number of services offered
Token systems always eliminate every form of delay
questions.e: The stated purpose of introducing tokens is to reduce waiting time. That purpose presupposes that waiting or queue management is a problem the office wants to improve. The statement does not imply that every visitor has an appointment or that all delays will disappear.

questions.topic: Three-set Venn diagram — inclusion and exclusion
questions.q: In a group, 30 people know Khasi, 25 know English and 20 know Hindi. Ten know Khasi and English, 8 know English and Hindi, 7 know Khasi and Hindi, and 3 know all three. How many know at least one of the languages?
questions.e: Apply inclusion–exclusion: 30 + 25 + 20 − 10 − 8 − 7 + 3. The pairwise intersections are subtracted because they were counted twice; the triple intersection is then added once because it was subtracted three times. The total is 53 people.

questions.q: Question: Is x greater than y? Statement I: x − y = 4. Statement II: x + y = 10. Which statement is sufficient by itself?
o: Statement I alone is sufficient
Statement II alone is sufficient
Both statements together are required
Neither statement is sufficient
questions.e: Statement I directly fixes the difference at a positive value, so x must be greater than y regardless of the individual values. Statement II alone permits several pairs, such as (6,4) and (4,6), so it cannot determine the comparison. Hence Statement I alone is sufficient.

questions.q: A town records unusually heavy rainfall for several days, followed by flooding in low-lying streets. Which inference is most directly supported?
o: The rainfall may have contributed to flooding, especially if drainage capacity was exceeded
The rainfall proves that every drain in town was blocked
Flooding must have occurred before the rainfall
The town's elevation changed during the rainfall
questions.e: The sequence and physical relationship support heavy rainfall as a plausible contributing cause of flooding, particularly where runoff exceeds drainage capacity. The facts do not prove that blocked drains were the only cause or establish unrelated changes such as altered elevation.

questions.q: What is the primary function of the Domain Name System (DNS) when a user enters a website's domain name?
o: It converts the domain name into an IP address used to locate the server
It encrypts every file stored on the server
It assigns a password to the user's browser
It compresses the website's images
questions.e: DNS is a distributed naming system that maps human-readable domain names to numerical Internet Protocol addresses. The browser can then use the address to connect to the relevant server. DNS does not itself encrypt website files or compress images.

questions.q: An employee wants the same mailbox folders and read/unread status to stay synchronised across a phone and a desktop. Which protocol is designed for this purpose?
o: SMTP
IMAP
FTP
DHCP
questions.e: IMAP allows a client to access and manipulate messages and remote mailboxes stored on a mail server, and it supports resynchronisation by offline clients. SMTP is used for mail submission or transfer, while FTP and DHCP serve different networking functions.

questions.q: In a database, an Orders table contains customer_id values that refer to rows in a Customers table. What is the main purpose of declaring customer_id as a foreign key?
o: To ensure that referenced customer records exist, preserving referential integrity
To encrypt the customer names automatically
To sort all orders by date
To make every order number unique without a separate constraint
questions.e: A foreign key constrains values in the referencing table to match an eligible key in the referenced table, subject to the database's rules. This preserves referential integrity by preventing an order from referring to a non-existent customer unless the relationship is handled through an allowed null or action.
questions.source: Original Practice — not an official PYQ. PostgreSQL 18 Documentation — Constraints and foreign keys.
questions.label: Original Practice
questions.sourceName: PostgreSQL 18 Documentation — Constraints and foreign keys

questions.q: A sender wants to encrypt a message so that only the intended recipient can decrypt it using public-key cryptography. Which key should the sender use to encrypt the message?
o: The sender's private key
The recipient's public key
The recipient's private key
A public key chosen by an unrelated third party
questions.e: For confidentiality in an asymmetric cryptosystem, the sender encrypts data with the recipient's public key. The corresponding private key, kept secret by the recipient, is used to decrypt it. Digital-signature workflows use the key pair in a different direction and serve authentication or integrity purposes.
questions.source: Original Practice — not an official PYQ. NIST Computer Security Resource Center — Public and Private Keys.
questions.label: Original Practice
questions.sourceName: NIST Computer Security Resource Center — Public and Private Keys

questions.q: What security properties does HTTPS obtain by using TLS for a web connection?
o: Confidentiality and integrity, with authentication of the server through its certificate
Guaranteed anonymity of every user
Automatic removal of malware from downloaded files
A guarantee that the website's business information is accurate
questions.e: TLS protects the connection by providing confidentiality and integrity and, in ordinary HTTPS use, authenticating the server through its certificate. It does not guarantee that a website's content is truthful, make users anonymous, or scan downloads for malware.

questions.q: What is a central purpose of virtual memory in a modern operating system?
o: To give each process a virtual address space that is mapped to physical memory and can be managed independently
To replace the CPU with a disk drive
To make every process share the same unrestricted physical addresses
To permanently store all program data in the BIOS
questions.e: Virtual memory gives a process its own address space and maps virtual addresses to physical pages. This abstraction supports isolation between processes and lets the operating system manage physical memory and paging without requiring programs to use raw physical addresses.

questions.q: Two tables are joined using INNER JOIN on a matching customer_id column. Which rows appear in the result?
o: Every row from the first table, whether matched or not
Only row pairs satisfying the join condition in both tables
Only rows that have no match in either table
A Cartesian product of every row in both tables
questions.e: An INNER JOIN returns combinations of rows for which the join condition evaluates to true. Rows without a match on the other side are excluded. A LEFT or RIGHT OUTER JOIN, unlike INNER JOIN, preserves unmatched rows from one specified side.
questions.source: Original Practice — not an official PYQ. PostgreSQL 18 Documentation — Joins Between Tables.
questions.label: Original Practice

questions.q: What is the principal constitutional task of a District Planning Committee under Article 243ZD?
o: To consolidate plans prepared by Panchayats and Municipalities and prepare a draft development plan for the district
To appoint judges of the district courts
To conduct elections to Parliament
To audit the accounts of the Union Government
questions.e: Article 243ZD provides for a District Planning Committee to consolidate plans prepared by Panchayats and Municipalities in the district and prepare a draft development plan for the district as a whole. The Constitution also specifies the composition and representation principles for the Committee.

questions.q: For what broad purpose may the President establish an Inter-State Council under Article 263?
o: To investigate and discuss subjects of common interest between the Union and States or among States, and make recommendations
To replace the Supreme Court in constitutional disputes
To prepare the annual Union Budget
To appoint Governors of all States
questions.e: Article 263 allows the President to establish an Inter-State Council when it appears that public interests would be served. Its functions can include investigating and discussing common-interest subjects, advising on disputes between States and making recommendations for better coordination.

questions.q: Under which constitutional article may a person be deprived of property only by authority of law?
o: Article 19
Article 21
Article 300A
Article 368
questions.e: Article 300A states that no person shall be deprived of property save by authority of law. The right to property is a constitutional right under this article, not one of the Fundamental Rights listed in Part III after the Forty-fourth Amendment removed the former Article 31.
questions.source: Original Practice — not an official PYQ. Government of India, Legislative Department — Constitution of India, 2024 edition.
questions.label: Original Practice

questions.q: Which dispute is within the Supreme Court's original jurisdiction under Article 131, subject to the article's conditions?
o: A private landlord's rent dispute with a tenant
A dispute between the Government of India and one or more States involving a legal right
An appeal against every decision of a municipal council
A criminal trial between two private citizens
questions.e: Article 131 gives the Supreme Court original jurisdiction in specified federal disputes involving the Government of India and States, or disputes between States, where the existence or extent of a legal right is involved. It is not a general jurisdiction over private disputes or ordinary local appeals.
questions.source: Original Practice — not an official PYQ. Government of India, Legislative Department — Constitution of India, 2024 edition.
questions.label: Original Practice
questions.sourceName: Government of India, Legislative Department — Constitution of India, 2024 edition

questions.q: What is the important difference between the subject-matter scope of Article 226 and Article 32 of the Constitution?
o: Article 226 permits High Courts to issue writs for Fundamental Rights and for any other purpose, while Article 32 concerns enforcement of Fundamental Rights
Article 226 is limited to criminal cases only
Article 32 gives High Courts jurisdiction over all civil disputes
Article 226 can be used only by the Union Government
questions.e: Article 226 empowers High Courts to issue writs for enforcement of Fundamental Rights and for other purposes. Article 32 is itself a Fundamental Right and empowers the Supreme Court to enforce Fundamental Rights. This makes Article 226 broader in subject matter, though it is discretionary.
questions.source: Original Practice — not an official PYQ. Government of India, Legislative Department — Constitution of India, 2024 edition.

questions.q: Who appoints the State Election Commissioner responsible for superintendence, direction and control of Panchayat elections under Article 243K?
o: The President of India
The Governor of the State
The Chief Justice of the High Court
The State Legislative Assembly Speaker
questions.e: Article 243K vests the appointment of the State Election Commissioner in the Governor. The State Election Commission supervises, directs and controls the preparation of electoral rolls and the conduct of Panchayat elections, subject to the constitutional safeguards for the Commissioner's tenure and removal.

questions.topic: Charter Act of 1813 — Company trade monopoly
questions.q: Which trading monopoly of the East India Company was ended by the Charter Act of 1813, while specified exceptions remained?
o: Its monopoly over trade with India, except the tea trade and trade with China
Its monopoly over trade with all of Europe
Its monopoly over the British domestic market
Its monopoly over the collection of land revenue in Bengal
questions.e: The Charter Act of 1813 ended the Company's commercial monopoly over trade with India, opening Indian trade to other British merchants. The Company retained its monopoly in the tea trade and trade with China, so the change was significant but not complete.

questions.topic: Subsidiary Alliance — obligations of Indian rulers
questions.q: Under Lord Wellesley's Subsidiary Alliance system, what was an Indian ruler generally required to do?
o: Accept a British force and meet its cost, while surrendering much independent control over external relations
Join a European military alliance chosen by the ruler without British consent
Abolish all local revenue collection
Transfer every village court to the East India Company
questions.e: A ruler accepting the Subsidiary Alliance had to maintain a British force at the State's expense, often through a subsidy or territorial cession. The ruler also accepted a British Resident and restrictions on independent diplomacy and military relations with other powers.
tags: Subsidiary Alliance — obligations of Indian rulers

questions.q: Which feature of the Rowlatt Act of 1919 became a major focus of opposition in India?
o: The power to detain people without trial in specified cases
The introduction of universal adult franchise
The abolition of the Indian Civil Service
The transfer of all provincial subjects to elected ministers
questions.e: The Rowlatt legislation extended extraordinary powers to the colonial government, including arrest and detention without ordinary trial safeguards in specified cases. Opposition to these repressive powers helped trigger the nationwide Rowlatt Satyagraha in 1919.
questions.source: Original Practice — not an official PYQ. NCERT — History Textbooks, including Modern Indian History.

questions.q: What was the principal constitutional task envisaged for the Constituent Assembly under the Cabinet Mission Plan of 1946?
o: To frame a constitution for India
To conduct the first general election under universal adult franchise
To appoint the first Governor-General of independent India
To divide all provinces into linguistic States immediately
questions.e: The Cabinet Mission Plan proposed a Constituent Assembly to frame the constitution of a united India, alongside a proposed structure of provincial groupings and an interim government. The Assembly's central task was constitution-making, not conducting the first general election.

questions.q: Which event in 1905 served as the immediate trigger for the Swadeshi Movement in Bengal?
o: The partition of Bengal by Lord Curzon
The Jallianwala Bagh massacre
The signing of the Gandhi–Irwin Pact
The launch of the Quit India Movement
questions.e: The partition of Bengal announced by Lord Curzon in 1905 provoked widespread opposition. The Swadeshi Movement encouraged the use of indigenous goods and the boycott of foreign goods, and became an important phase of anti-colonial mobilisation.

questions.q: What issue lay at the centre of the Ilbert Bill controversy in British India?
o: Whether Indian judges could try European British subjects in criminal cases
Whether Indians could vote in the British Parliament
Whether the East India Company could resume trade in tea
Whether the British Crown could abolish all princely States
questions.e: The Ilbert Bill sought to remove a racial legal distinction by allowing qualified Indian judges and magistrates to try European British subjects in criminal cases. Strong opposition from many Europeans in India exposed the racial inequalities embedded in colonial administration.

questions.q: Western Disturbances that bring winter rain and mountain snowfall to parts of northern India generally originate in which region?
o: The Mediterranean–Caspian region
The equatorial Pacific
The South China Sea
The southern Indian Ocean
questions.e: The India Meteorological Department describes Western Disturbances as extratropical systems originating around the Mediterranean or Caspian Sea and travelling east through West Asia. They bring important winter precipitation to north-western India and snowfall in the western Himalaya.

questions.q: Why does the leeward side of a mountain range commonly receive less rainfall in a rain-shadow situation?
o: Air descends after losing much of its moisture on the windward side and warms as it descends
The leeward side is always closer to the equator
Mountains absorb all sunlight before it reaches the leeward slope
The leeward side has no atmospheric pressure
questions.e: Moist air is forced upward on the windward slope, cools and releases precipitation. After crossing the crest, the air descends, warms and becomes relatively drier, so less condensation and rainfall occur on the leeward side. This creates a rain-shadow region.
questions.source: Original Practice — not an official PYQ. NCERT — Fundamentals of Physical Geography textbook portal.

questions.q: In a mature soil profile, which horizon is commonly associated with the accumulation of materials such as clay and iron leached from upper layers?
o: O horizon
A horizon
B horizon
R horizon
questions.e: The B horizon is commonly described as the zone of accumulation or illuviation. Materials leached from upper horizons, including clay and compounds of iron or aluminium, may accumulate there. The O horizon is organic litter, while the A horizon is topsoil.
questions.source: Original Practice — not an official PYQ. NCERT — Fundamentals of Physical Geography textbook portal.

questions.q: On a topographic map with a constant contour interval, what do closely spaced contour lines indicate?
o: A steep slope
A perfectly flat plain
A river flowing at constant speed
A change in political boundary
questions.e: Contour lines join points of equal elevation. When successive contours are close together, elevation changes over a short horizontal distance, indicating a steep slope. Widely spaced contours usually indicate a gentler slope.
questions.source: Original Practice — not an official PYQ. NCERT — Fundamentals of Physical Geography textbook portal.

questions.q: What is the usual direct thermal effect of a cold ocean current on nearby coastal areas?
o: It lowers the temperature of adjacent coastal air and water
It raises coastal water temperature throughout the year
It stops all evaporation from the ocean
It changes the latitude of the coastline
questions.e: Cold currents transport relatively cool water and can lower the temperature of adjacent coastal air and water. Their effects on rainfall vary with local winds and atmospheric conditions, so the safest general inference is the cooling effect rather than an absolute claim about rainfall.
questions.source: Original Practice — not an official PYQ. NCERT — Fundamentals of Physical Geography textbook portal.

questions.q: At the same season and time of day, why does the Sun's noon altitude generally become lower as an observer moves from the equator towards a pole?
o: The Sun's rays strike more obliquely, spreading energy over a larger area
The Earth stops rotating at higher latitudes
The atmosphere becomes completely absent near the poles
The Sun moves closer to the equator during the day
questions.e: Because of the Earth's curvature and axial tilt, the Sun's rays generally arrive at a lower angle at higher latitudes for the same season. More oblique rays spread the same incoming energy over a larger surface area, reducing the intensity received per unit area.
questions.source: Original Practice — not an official PYQ. NCERT — Fundamentals of Physical Geography textbook portal.
questions.label: Original Practice

questions.q: In the Union Budget's standard presentation, what does the fiscal deficit measure?
o: Total expenditure minus total receipts excluding debt-capital receipts
Revenue expenditure minus revenue receipts only
Interest payments minus tax revenue
Total tax revenue minus capital expenditure
questions.e: The Union Budget defines fiscal deficit as total expenditure less total receipts excluding debt-capital receipts. It reflects the Government's total borrowing requirement. It is therefore broader than the revenue deficit, which compares revenue expenditure with revenue receipts.

questions.q: What is meant by a revenue deficit in government budgeting?
o: Revenue expenditure exceeds revenue receipts
Capital expenditure exceeds capital receipts
Tax revenue exceeds total expenditure
Borrowings exceed interest payments
questions.e: Revenue deficit is the excess of revenue expenditure over revenue receipts. It indicates that current revenue receipts are insufficient to meet revenue-account expenditure. It is distinct from fiscal deficit, which also reflects the Government's overall borrowing requirement.
questions.source: Original Practice — not an official PYQ. Union Budget 2025–26 — Budget at a Glance.

questions.q: Which combination best describes stagflation?
o: High inflation together with stagnant economic activity and weak employment
Falling prices with rapid output growth
High output growth with zero unemployment and stable prices
A temporary rise in exports with a balanced budget
questions.e: Stagflation combines persistent inflation with stagnating output or economic growth and often elevated unemployment. It is difficult for policymakers because measures that restrain inflation may further weaken activity, while measures that stimulate demand can add to price pressure.
questions.source: Original Practice — not an official PYQ. NCERT — Economics Textbook Portal.

questions.topic: Price elasticity of demand — percentage method
questions.q: If a 10% increase in price causes quantity demanded to fall by 20%, what is the absolute value of price elasticity of demand using the percentage method?
questions.e: Price elasticity of demand is the percentage change in quantity demanded divided by the percentage change in price, using absolute values when asked for magnitude. Here 20% ÷ 10% = 2, so demand is elastic over the stated change.
tags: Price elasticity of demand — percentage method

questions.q: In the simplest textbook deposit-creation model with no currency leakage and no excess reserves, what determines the deposit multiplier?
o: The reciprocal of the required reserve ratio
The sum of the reserve ratio and inflation rate
The reciprocal of the tax-to-GDP ratio
The amount of currency held by the government alone
questions.e: In the simplified model, the deposit multiplier equals 1 divided by the required reserve ratio. This result assumes banks lend all excess reserves and the public holds no additional currency; real-world money creation is affected by behaviour, regulation and demand for credit.

questions.q: Which cell-division process reduces the chromosome number by half to produce haploid cells for sexual reproduction?
o: Mitosis
Meiosis
Binary fission
Budding
questions.e: Meiosis involves two successive divisions following one round of DNA replication and produces cells with half the chromosome number of the parent cell. This reduction is important because fertilisation combines haploid gametes and restores the diploid chromosome number.

questions.q: What is osmosis?
o: Net movement of water through a selectively permeable membrane from higher water potential to lower water potential
Movement of solute particles from low concentration to high concentration using ATP
Movement of all gases only through a cell wall
Random movement of solid particles without a concentration gradient
questions.e: Osmosis is the net movement of water across a selectively permeable membrane down a water-potential gradient. In a simple solution comparison, water moves from the more dilute side towards the more concentrated side until equilibrium is approached.
questions.source: Original Practice — not an official PYQ. NCERT — Biology Textbook Portal.

questions.q: A ray of light passes obliquely from air into ordinary glass. What happens at the boundary?
o: Its speed decreases and the ray bends towards the normal
Its speed increases and the ray bends away from the normal
Its speed and direction remain unchanged in every case
It is converted entirely into sound
questions.e: Glass has a higher refractive index than air. When light enters it obliquely, its speed decreases and the ray bends towards the normal. The frequency remains unchanged across the boundary, while wavelength decreases in the slower medium.
questions.source: Original Practice — not an official PYQ. NCERT — Biology Textbook Portal.
questions.label: Original Practice

questions.q: Why is a pyramid of energy always upright in a natural ecosystem?
o: Energy is lost at each trophic transfer, so less energy is available at higher levels
Predators always outnumber producers
Energy is created at every trophic level
Decomposers return all energy to the Sun
questions.e: Only a fraction of energy stored at one trophic level is transferred to the next; much is used in metabolism and dissipated as heat. Consequently, the energy available to higher trophic levels decreases, keeping the energy pyramid upright.

questions.q: In carbon mineralisation, how can carbon dioxide become stored in a stable mineral form?
o: It reacts with suitable calcium-, magnesium- or iron-rich silicate rocks to form carbonate minerals
It is converted directly into atmospheric nitrogen
It evaporates into space without chemical change
It becomes liquid oxygen inside sedimentary rocks
questions.e: The USGS describes carbon mineralisation as a reaction in which CO₂ interacts with suitable silicate rocks rich in elements such as calcium, magnesium or iron and precipitates carbonate minerals. This can lock carbon into a solid mineral form for long-term geological storage.

questions.q: Why can excessive nutrient input into a lake lead to fish deaths?
o: Algal growth and subsequent microbial decomposition can consume dissolved oxygen
Nutrients immediately remove all salts from the lake
Algae permanently stop sunlight from reaching the atmosphere
The lake's water becomes pure distilled water
questions.e: Excess nitrogen or phosphorus can stimulate algal blooms. When algae die, microbial decomposition uses dissolved oxygen; in poorly mixed or stratified water this can create hypoxic conditions that stress or kill fish and other aquatic organisms.

o: West Jaintia Hills
Ri-Bhoi
East Khasi Hills
South Garo Hills
